Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation in this sequence has a cost of |E|, which occurs when the selected vertex is connected to every other vertex in the graph. The average amortized cost of the sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis is |E| / |V|.

*   In the context of an adjacency list, the cost associated with processing a vertex v is defined as the number of edges originating from v, denoted as out-degree(v).
*   To find the average amortized cost, we sum the costs of all |V| operations (which equals the total number of edges |E|) and divide by the number of operations |V|.
